question: does the productized v13 entity-hub recipe lift the write_text product path on the multi-session pool?
design: full-population paired A/B on all 133 multi-session questions: identical seeding (write_text per [sid @ date] session text), identical orchestration; the hubs arm additionally attributes paragraphs to sessions and runs build_entity_hubs (MEMPLEX_ENTITY_HUBS=1, glm-5.3 extraction thinking-disabled) before the query. Both arms glm-5.3 answerer/judge, fallback paragraph composition, MPS device (same instrument as the archived probes). Quota abort wired before the full run; resume rode out 7 environment kills (client restarts) with zero loss.
findings: The productized hub recipe EXCEEDS its harness effect on the same pool: +9.8pp paired vs the harness's +6.8pp - the product path (write_text -> paragraphs -> hubs) benefits even more than the harness seeding did, because flat retrieval was the product's bottleneck on this pool.
18 up / 5 down: the flip ratio stabilizes the verdict well beyond noise (the delta never left positive territory after n=27 and settled into the +8-10pp band from n=57).

J-scale projection: multi-session is 133/500 of LongMemEval-J, so +9.8pp on this pool is worth ~+2.6pp overall - the single largest product-path lever measured to date (previous best: paragraph-primary fusion's pool gain).

Composition note: both arms ran fallback composition, so absolute numbers are not comparable to the 0.7669 primary-fusion reading; the paired delta is composition-robust. The primary-composition hub run is the follow-up that sets the official product-path number.
honest_reading: paired same-questions A/B, same answerer/judge family; hub extraction itself is glm-3.3-family LLM output (the recipe's known dependence); the 7 environment kills during the run were absorbed by per-question jsonl resume (records never regressed); no quota interruption (abort never fired).
